A Chrome probe shows getComputedStyle(el,'::before') returns resolved px for width/right, resolves attr(), but returns content as the literal 'counter(s, upper-roman) ". yo"' (counters are not resolved).
rootCause: ui.html pageAgent: walk()/childrenOf()/gatherRuns() iterate el.childNodes only. Pseudo-elements are not DOM nodes and have no rect, and css(el, pseudo) is never called for ::before/::after. Range.getClientRects() in textGeometry/lineCount also skips generated content.
fix: Add materializePseudos() to pageAgent. Call it inside the message handler after the SECOND settle() and immediately before extract(opts), so the layout is final (fonts, images and lazy content are done). Never call it before scrolling or settling: the snapshot copies used px values. 1) READ phase, with no DOM writes. For each el in body.querySelectorAll('*'), skipping SKIP_TAGS and elements already display:none, and for each p in ['::before', '::after']: - pcs = getComputedStyle(el, p). Skip it if pcs.content is 'none' or 'normal', or pcs.display is 'none'. - Snapshot decl = {prop: pcs.getPropertyValue(prop)} for every prop in pcs except 'content'. - Resolve content into parts. Quoted strings become text (CSS escapes are already decoded). attr(x) becomes el.getAttribute(x). open-quote/close-quote come from pcs.quotes, with 'auto' meaning “ ” ‘ ’, plus a depth counter. url(u) becomes an . - counter(name[,style]) and counters(name, sep[,style]) come from an emulated counter table. Build it in document order before this loop: for each element and its ::before/::after, apply counterReset, then counterSet, then counterIncrement, using the computed values with nested scopes per subtree. Add the implicit list-item counter for display:list-item. Format these styles: decimal, decimal-leading-zero, lower-/upper-roman, lower-/upper-alpha/latin and lower-greek. Use decimal as the fallback. - Record oof = pcs.position is 'absolute' or 'fixed'. 2) WRITE phase for in-flow pseudos (oof false: inline text like '/mo', ' *', ' →'; flex/grid dividers; display:block underlines): - Snapshot the rects of el, el.parentElement and all of el's element children. - Create , apply s.style.setProperty(k, v, 'important') for each decl, and append the parts. - Insert it with el.insertBefore(s, el.firstChild) for ::before, or el.appendChild(s) for ::after. Set data-h2f-b or data-h2f-a on el. - Inject one stylesheet: [data-h2f-b]::before,[data-h2f-a]::after{content:none!important}. - After all writes, recompare the snapshotted rects with a 0.5px tolerance. For any host whose own rect or any original child's rect drifted, a structural selector fired. Revert that host: remove its spans and its data-h2f-* attribute, so the original pseudo renders again and is skipped as it is today. Repeat once to settle the cascade. 3) Out-of-flow pseudos (absolute/fixed: blobs, overlays, badges, dots, abs underlines, Flowbite toggle knobs): - Never insert them into the host, because that changes :last-child, :first-child and + selectors. - Instead, append an to document.documentElement after , with position:absolute and pointer-events:none. Place it exactly over the pseudo's containing block's padding box: the nearest ancestor-or-self of el with position other than static, or with transform/filter/contain. For fixed, use the viewport rect plus scroll. Use page coordinates of getBoundingClientRect, inset by the border widths, and set the proxy's position:relative. - Put the materialized span inside it; the copied resolved px insets reproduce the exact placement. Add the same content:none stylesheet attribute on the host. - Store S.pseudo.set(el, {before: [proxySpan], after: [proxySpan]}) and mark the proxies with data-h2f-skip so childrenOf/walk ignore them. - This also covers replaced hosts, such as INPUT with appearance:none, which can't take children. formNode then appends those layers too. 4) Integrate the out-of-flow proxies in walk(el). Let pb = layers from walking each S.pseudo.get(el).before span, and pa likewise for after, positioned with ox/oy = rect.left/top of el. - Frame case: kids = pb.concat(childrenOf(...), pa). This follows paint order: ::before is under the children, ::after is above. Force a frame (not the plain-wrapper or lifted path) when pb or pa is non-empty. Also include them when computing `overflows`, so clip is kept for the hero blob. - Text-block case: if el or any descendant inside the text block has proxies, wrap the TEXT in a frame (no fills) and add the pseudo layers as absolute siblings. Without this, .hl::after inside an h1 is lost. - In nameFor, name these layers `${tag}::before` or `${tag}::after`. 5) Ship this together with: (a) Icon-font handling. When a pseudo's text is in the PUA (U+E000–U+F8FF or U+F0000+), or its font family is a known icon font, draw it to a canvas with ctx.font from the resolved font shorthand (the webfont is loaded in the iframe) and emit an IMAGE layer instead of TEXT. Otherwise Figma substitutes a font and shows tofu. (b) Negative z-index. Before materializing, skip any oof pseudo with zIndex < 0 when a painting ancestor would cover it in the browser: walk ancestors up to the nearest stacking context (z-index not auto, opacity < 1, transform, etc.). If any ancestor strictly inside that context has a non-transparent background, the pseudo was hidden, so drop it. Otherwise insert it as the first layer of that stacking-context frame. No new Figma API is needed. The output is the existing FRAME, TEXT, RECT and IMAGE nodes, so code.js stays unchanged and ES2017 is unaffected.

title: ::before/::after (and list markers) are never extracted: decorative dots, overlays, separators and checkmarks disappear
evidence: layout-flex-variants: the 16px indigo circles from .plan li::before are all red in diff.png. layout-mobile-app: the .card::after translucent circle is missing in render.png. layout-legacy-structures: the breadcrumb separators from a:after{content:' /'} are lost ('Home Reports Q3'), and ol.steps loses its '1. 2. 3.' markers (TEXT nodes only, pl=20).
rootCause: ui.html walk()/isTextBlock()/gatherRuns() iterate only el.childNodes. Pseudo-elements and ::marker are not in the DOM, and css(el, pseudo) is only used for ::placeholder.
fix:
A. Turn pseudo-elements into real probe elements before measuring (ui.html, pageAgent: new function materializePseudos(), called at the top of extract() before any css()/walk(); a matching restore runs in a finally block after the tree is built).

1. Inject one style element:
   `h2f-pseudo{display:inline}[data-h2f-b]::before{content:none!important}[data-h2f-a]::after{content:none!important}`

2. For every element in document.body.querySelectorAll('*'), skipping SKIP_TAGS and form controls, and for each p of ['::before', '::after']:
   - Read pcs = getComputedStyle(el, p).
   - Skip when pcs.content is 'none' or 'normal' or pcs.display is 'none'.
   - Create a probe: `document.createElement('h2f-pseudo')`. A custom tag means tag and class selectors cannot match it.
   - Copy the computed style: `for (const prop of pcs) if (prop !== 'content' && !/^(transition|animation)/.test(prop)) probe.style.setProperty(prop, pcs.getPropertyValue(prop));`
   - Fill it from parseContent(pcs.content, el, pcs):
     - Tokenize top-level parts.
     - Strings: strip the quotes and unescape `\\([0-9a-f]{1,6}) ?` with String.fromCodePoint.
     - attr(x) becomes el.getAttribute(x) || ''.
     - open-quote / close-quote become '“' / '”'.
     - counter(name[, style]) / counters(): number = 1 + the count of el's preceding siblings, or the preceding siblings of the nearest ancestor that has the counter-increment, whose computed counterIncrement names `name`. Stop at the element whose counterReset names it. Format with decimal, decimal-leading-zero, lower/upper-alpha or lower/upper-roman.
     - url(...) or a gradient: set probe.style.backgroundImage to it, with backgroundSize '100% 100%' and the width/height from pcs. walk() then emits a normal frame with an image or gradient fill.
     - Set probe.textContent to the joined text.
   - Insert it: as the first child for ::before (el.insertBefore(probe, el.firstChild)), as the last child for ::after.
   - Mark the element with el.setAttribute('data-h2f-b' or 'data-h2f-a', '').

3. Selector side-effect guard. Before inserting probes into an element, record el.getBoundingClientRect() and the rects of its element children. After inserting that element's probes, force layout and compare. If any rect moved or resized by more than 1px (Tailwind space-y, :first-child, :empty and so on), remove the probes, clear the data attributes, and skip that element. This means the pseudo is lost on that element, but the page is never corrupted.

4. Icon-font guard. If every character of the content is in the Private Use Area (U+E000–U+F8FF, or plane 15/16), or the font family matches /awesome|icons|material|bootstrap-icons|remixicon/i, do not emit text. Rasterize the glyph instead: draw it with ctx.font = `${weight} ${size} ${family}` and ctx.fillStyle = color on a canvas the size of the probe (the font is already loaded in the iframe). Set the PNG data URL as the probe's background-image and leave textContent empty, so it becomes an image-filled frame.

5. In nameFor(), name probes '::before' / '::after'. Remove all probes and data attributes in extract()'s finally block. No change is needed in walk(), isTextBlock(), gatherRuns(), toSegments() or code.js. Inline probes join text blocks with their own computed style, absolute probes get `absolute: true`, and in-flow block or flex probes become regular children that the auto-layout detection already handles.

B. List markers (ui.html walk(), plus a helper markerNode(li, ox, oy)).

For an element with cs.display === 'list-item':
- Compute mcs = getComputedStyle(el, '::marker').
- Skip it when listStyleType is 'none' and listStyleImage is 'none', or when mcs.content is 'none'.

Marker text:
- If mcs.content is a string, use that string.
- Otherwise use the list-style-type:
  - disc '•', circle '◦', square '▪'
  - decimal, alpha or roman get the ordinal plus '.'
  - the ordinal is li.value when the attribute is set, otherwise ol.start ± the index among li siblings (minus when ol.reversed)
  - a quoted string type uses that string
- list-style-image becomes a small image RECT instead.

Position:
- list-style-position 'inside': insert it as an inline h2f-pseudo probe at the start during the pre-pass from section A, styled from mcs (color, font weight, font size), and suppress the real marker with `[data-h2f-m]{list-style-type:none!important}`. The guard from step A.3 applies here too.
- 'outside': do not touch the DOM.
  - Measure the text width w with canvas measureText, using mcs's font, without the trailing space.
  - Get the first line box from a Range over el's contents (first client rect with width > 0).
  - Emit a TEXT node with segments from segStyle(el, mcs) and textAlign RIGHT.
  - Set w = w + 1, x = (el's border-box left − spaceWidth − w) − ox, y = line top − oy, h = line height.
  - Mark it absolute: true so tryAutoLayout ignores it and code.js gives it layoutPositioning 'ABSOLUTE'.
  - walk() returns [markerNode, ...liNodes] for that li.

Do not use setRangeListOptions for per-li text nodes. Each node would restart numbering at 1, and Figma's own list indent would shift the measured text.
verifierNotes:
Confirmed. In ui.html, pageAgent's walk(), childrenOf(), isTextBlock() and gatherRuns() only iterate el.childNodes. css(el, pseudo) is used only for '::placeholder' in formNode(). Nothing reads ::before, ::after or ::marker, so whatever they draw never reaches the tree.

What I checked:
- Re-ran layout-legacy-structures (diff 1.25%). The tree's TEXT nodes read "Home" / "Reports" with no " /" separators from `.crumbs a:after{content:" /"}`. The ol.steps items are bare text with no "1. 2. 3." markers.
- Re-ran layout-flex-variants (diff 0.85%). In render.png the 16px indigo dots from `.plan li::before` are missing, and diff.png shows them as solid red circles.
- The existing dev/out/gen-pseudo-decor render loses all of these:
  - hero glow and gradient bar
  - green status dot
  - title underline bar
  - numbered step badges built with counter()
  - "Popular" badge
  - "/mo" suffix
  - big quote mark
  - divider lines
  - breadcrumb "/" separators
  - required "*"
  - " →" arrows
  - dark gradient overlay on the image card, which leaves white text on a bright photo
- gen-lists covers ::marker / list-style. The code has no marker logic at all.

These patterns are everywhere in AI-generated CSS: decorative blobs, overlays, checkmarks, separators and badges. That makes this high severity.

Problems with the proposed fix:
1. Setting el.dataset.h2fSkip does nothing by itself. Unless a stylesheet actually turns the real pseudo off, the page gets laid out with the pseudo twice: once real, once as the probe.
2. Inserting an extra child can change which elements CSS selectors match:
   - :first-child, :last-child, :only-child, :empty, nth-child
   - sibling combinators. Tailwind v3 space-y uses `> :not([hidden]) ~ :not([hidden])` and v4 uses `> :not(:last-child)`.
   
   So a ::before or ::after probe can add or remove margins on the real children and silently move the page. This needs a check, and a rollback when the check fails.
3. Copying 'content' onto a real element is risky: content:url() turns an element into a replaced element. The probe also has to handle counter()/counters(), attr(), open-quote/close-quote, CSS escapes and url()/gradient content. counter() numbering ("01", "1.") is very common.
4. The proposal runs probes per element inside walk(). Running them as a pre-pass is simpler and safer: walk(), isTextBlock(), gatherRuns(), tryAutoLayout() then work unchanged, because probes are ordinary elements with inline styles. That covers inline text pseudos (" /", " →", " *"), block bars, flex:1 divider lines and absolute overlays. The separate gatherRuns change is unnecessary.
5. setRangeListOptions is the wrong tool here. walk() turns each li into its own TEXT node, so ORDERED would show "1." on every item. Figma also adds its own list indent, which shifts the measured text. Markers should be separate positioned TEXT layers.
6. Regression risk: icon fonts (Font Awesome, Bootstrap Icons) draw via ::before using Private Use Area glyphs. Turned into Figma text, they would render as tofu boxes (empty placeholder squares) or nothing, so they need special handling.

title: List markers (::marker) are dropped: bullets, numbers, alpha/roman, colored markers, list-style-image, string markers and the <summary> disclosure triangles
evidence: gen-lists.render.png: every bullet and number is missing (disc/circle/square, 1. 2. 3., start=7 with blue ::marker, a./b., I./II./III., the orange list-style-image squares, inside markers, '👉 ' ::marker content, the '— ' string marker). No marker glyph exists in gen-lists.json. gen-tw-controls: Tailwind 'list-disc list-inside marker:text-indigo-500' and 'list-decimal marker:text-slate-400' are lost. gen-forms: the ▼/▶ triangles of the <details><summary> are lost. A Chrome probe returns content 'normal' for getComputedStyle(li,'::marker') and li.value === 0 when there is no value attribute, so the ordinal has to be computed.
rootCause: ui.html pageAgent: nothing reads display:list-item, listStyleType, listStyleImage, listStylePosition or the ::marker style. walk() only sees the li's child nodes. Outside markers never take layout space, so they vanish without a trace. Inside markers leave a gap before the text (textGeometry measures the text, not the marker).
fix:
This is the corrected fix. Outside markers are measured with a probe that is removed right away, so the DOM stays unchanged and isTextBlock is unaffected. Inside markers become real inline text. 1) Pre-pass in extract(), before any walk(). Set S.markers = new WeakMap(). For each el in body.querySelectorAll('*'), skip it unless /list-item/.test(css(el).display) and it is visible. Then: - ms = getComputedStyle(el,'::marker'); lst = css(el).listStyleType; img = css(el).listStyleImage. - Marker text: - If /^["']/.test(ms.content), take that string, unquoted. - Else if img !== 'none' and it parses as url(...), use an image marker. - Else if lst is a quoted string, use the unquoted string. - Else if lst === 'none', skip this element. - Else use fmt(ordinal(el), lst) + suffix. The suffix is '. ' for numeric and alphabetic types, ' ' for disc/circle/square/disclosure-*. - fmt covers: - decimal and decimal-leading-zero - lower/upper-alpha|latin (bijective base 26) - lower/upper-roman - lower-greek - disc '•', circle '◦', square '▪' - disclosure-open '▾', disclosure-closed '▸' - anything else falls back to decimal. - ordinal(el): - p = el.parentElement; sibs = p's element children with display list-item. - rev = p.tagName === 'OL' && p.reversed. - base = p.tagName === 'OL' ? (p.hasAttribute('start') ? p.start : (rev ? sibs.length : 1)) : 1. - Walk sibs in order: n = (i === 0) ? base : n + (rev ? -1 : 1). A sibling with a value attribute sets n = parseInt(value). - Return n for el. Don't use li.value, which is 0 without the attribute. - Position 'inside' (css(el).listStylePosition === 'inside'): - Prepend a real inline span with white-space:pre. Copy color, font-family, font-size, font-weight and font-style from ms. Use the text, or for an image marker an sized like the browser's (its natural size). - Set el.style.listStyleType = 'none' and el.style.listStyleImage = 'none'. - Layout is unchanged because the inside marker was already an inline box of that text. The span becomes the first segment of the li's TEXT through gatherRuns, so the gap disappears. - Do all inside insertions in the pre-pass, before any measurement. - Position 'outside': - s = with the same font and color copied from ms, holding the text or an . - el.prepend(s); r = s.getBoundingClientRect(); s.remove(). - Store S.markers.set(el, { box: r, segs, image }). For text, segs = toSegments-style segment built with segStyle(el, ms) with decoration forced to null. For an image, store an IMAGE fill via imageRef(url, null). - The probe gives the browser's marker box: right edge = content start, top = first line-box top. This held for plain text, a block

child, and a 20px li. - Markers on

(Chrome gives it display:list-item with disclosure-open/closed) are handled by the same path. Skip the element if getComputedStyle(el,'::-webkit-details-marker').display === 'none', or if Tailwind's list-none set lst to none. 2) Emit the markers in walk(el, ox, oy). Look up m = S.markers.get(el). When it is set, build mk: - For text: mk = textNode(m.segs, {x: m.box.left, y: m.box.top, w: m.box.width, h: m.box.height, align: 'RIGHT', autoResize: 'WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT'}). - For an image: mk = a RECT with the IMAGE fill. - Set mk.absolute = true and mk.name = 'marker'. Then: - Text-block path without a visual: shift(t, ox, oy); shift(mk, ox, oy); return [t, mk]. The marker is an absolute sibling. The parent ul's tryAutoLayout already ignores absolute kids (`frame.children.filter((k) => !k.absolute)`), and code.js applies layoutPositioning='ABSOLUTE' only when the parent is auto layout. The li stays one TEXT, so rich inline text is kept. - Frame paths (text block with a visual, or a generic frame): shift(mk, rect.left, rect.top) and push it into the frame's children before tryAutoLayout. A negative x is fine because frames clip only when overflow is set, which matches Chrome: an overflow:hidden li also clips its outside marker. - Plain-wrapper reduction (kids.length === 1): count kids before adding the marker. If the li gets reduced to its single child, return [child, mk], with mk shifted by (ox, oy). 3) Optional, off by default: a native-list mode for simple lists only. These are ul/ol whose li are pure text blocks, with type disc or decimal, start 1, not reversed, marker color equal to the text color, position outside, and no nesting. Emit one TEXT with '\n'-joined paragraphs and per-paragraph list types. In code.js, after the fonts load, call t.setRangeListOptions(s, e, {type: 'UNORDERED'|'ORDERED'}) and set t.listSpacing to the measured gap between items. Keep step 2 as the default for geometric fidelity. Out of scope here: ::before/::after content and CSS counter() resolution. They are also dropped today (the ✓ badges and the counter-list numbers in gen-lists) and need their own fix. Counter emulation belongs there, not in the marker fix.

title: List markers (bullets / numbers from ::marker) are not exported
evidence: text-tw-pricing.render.png (1440 and 390): `list-disc marker:text-indigo-500` and `list-decimal` lists show items with no bullets or numbers ('5 projects', 'Unlimited projects' etc. float with a 20px gap). Feature and pricing lists are on almost every landing page.
rootCause: ui.html walk()/gatherRuns() only read DOM text nodes. Elements with display:list-item and list-style-type≠none never produce marker content, and ::marker is not measurable via getBoundingClientRect.
fix:
In ui.html (pageAgent):

1) Add `markerNode(el, cs)`, which returns a TEXT layer in page coordinates, or null.

Skip conditions: return null if `cs.display` does not include 'list-item', if box.h < 0.5, or if ::marker content is 'none' or '""'. Get the marker style with `const ms = css(el, '::marker')`; Chrome supports getComputedStyle with '::marker'.

Marker text:
- `ms.content` set and not 'normal' (a quoted string): strip the quotes and use it.
- `listStyleImage !== 'none'`: return `{type:'RECT', fills:[imagePaint(imageRef(url))]}` sized to the image's natural size, or skip it.
- `listStyleType` is a quoted string (e.g. `"— "`): strip the quotes and use the string as-is, with no suffix.
- disc → '• ', circle → '◦ ', square → '▪ ', disclosure-closed → '▸ ', disclosure-open → '▾ ', none → null.
- Counter types (decimal, decimal-leading-zero, lower/upper-alpha|latin, lower/upper-roman, lower-greek): use `fmt(n) + '. '`. To compute n:
  - Let `p = el.parentElement` and `items` = the sibling elements whose display is list-item.
  - Let `rev = p.tagName === 'OL' && p.reversed`, `step = rev ? -1 : 1`.
  - Set `n = (p.hasAttribute('start') ? p.start : (rev ? items.length : 1)) - step`.
  - For each item up to and including el: `n = it.hasAttribute('value') ? it.value : n + step`.
  - Implement fmt for alpha (bijective base 26) and roman (standard table). Fall back to decimal for anything else.

This depends on pseudo-element materialization in `walk()` and `childrenOf()`. For each element, read `pcs = css(el, '::before')` and `css(el, '::after')`. Skip it if `pcs.content` is `none`, `normal`, a `url(...)`, or `""`. Otherwise turn `content` from a CSS string into plain text: strip the quotes and unescape. Computed style already returns the real character, so `"\f00c"` comes back as `'""'`. Handle `attr()` and `counter()` best-effort.

1. **Classifier.**
   ```
   const PUA = /^[\s-\u{F0000}-\u{FFFFD}\u{100000}-\u{10FFFD}]+$/u;
   const ICON_FAM = /material (icons|symbols)|font ?awesome|bootstrap-icons|remixicon|ionicons|feather|phosphor|tabler|boxicons|line ?awesome|icomoon|glyphicons|fontello|themify|simple-line-icons|lucide/i;
   isIcon(text, cs) = PUA.test(text) || ICON_FAM.test(parseFamilies(cs.fontFamily)[0] || '')
   ```
   Apply it in two places:
   - to pseudo content;
   - in `isTextBlock()`/`blockText()`, when the whole text of the element is one short run (at most about 3 words) and its first family matches.

2. **Icon node `iconNode(el, text, cs, box)`.** Here `box` is the element's border box for a pseudo-only `<i>`, or the text range rect for real text nodes.
   - Rasterize at `k = 4`. Make a canvas of `ceil(box.w*k) × ceil(box.h*k)`, then `ctx.scale(k,k)`.
   - Set `ctx.font = cs.fontStyle + ' ' + cs.fontWeight + ' ' + cs.fontSize + ' ' + cs.fontFamily`, `ctx.fillStyle = cs.color`, and `ctx.textBaseline = 'alphabetic'`.
   - Set `if ('letterSpacing' in ctx) ctx.letterSpacing = cs.letterSpacing`.
   - Measure with `m = ctx.measureText(text)`, and let `A = m.fontBoundingBoxAscent`, `D = m.fontBoundingBoxDescent`.
   - Use the line height `lh = parseFloat(cs.lineHeight)`, or `A + D` when it is `normal`.
   - **Vertical:** the baseline is at `by = (lh - (A + D)) / 2 + A`, measured from the top of the line box. When `box` came from a Range rect, it is `by = A`, because the Range covers exactly the content area.
   - **Horizontal:** `bx = 0` for start/left, `(box.w - m.width) / 2` for center, `box.w - m.width` for right/end. Use the text-align of the element that holds the glyph, inside its content box. This is what centers `.nav i { width: 18px; text-align: center }`.
   - Call `ctx.fillText(text, bx, by)`.
   - Emit:
     ```
     {type:'RECT', name:'icon · ' + firstIconClass(el), x, y, w, h,
      fills:[{type:'IMAGE', ref:imageRef(canvas.toDataURL('image/png'), null), scaleMode:'FILL'}],
      iconText:{chars:text, families:parseFamilies(cs.fontFamily), weight, italic, size, color:solid(parseColor(cs.color)), align}}
     ```

   - Wrap `toDataURL` in try/catch. If it fails, emit `iconText` only.

4. **`prepareFonts`.** Collect `iconText` specs as well. Expose `exact(spec)`, which is true when `idx.has(spec.families[0].toLowerCase())`, the family is not a generic alias, and loading it did not fail.

5. **Building the node.** When a RECT has `iconText` and `exact(iconText)` is true:

   - This keeps Material Icons and Material Symbols editable, since Figma ships them as Google Fonts and its text applies ligatures.
   - Otherwise keep the image RECT. If there is no image either, draw nothing; never fall back to Inter for an icon.

6. **Fallback for icon-classified TEXT.** For a TEXT segment that the agent marked as an icon (`seg.icon = true`), don't substitute Inter when the family is missing. Use the agent's raster instead.

**Optional follow-up**

Re-fetch the `@font-face` `src`. cdnjs and fonts.gstatic send CORS headers. Parse the font with an inlined opentype.js and emit an SVG path filled with `cs.color`, so icons stay recolourable vectors.

- Nothing in pageAgent reads cs.zIndex, isolation or any other stacking-context trigger.

- ::before/::after are not extracted at all yet (css(el, pseudo) is only used for ::placeholder). For gen-pseudo-decor and gen-tw-controls the problem is therefore hidden today; it would only appear once pseudo-elements are materialized. 1. It reads only `cs.transform`. Accept these computed forms: 'Npx', 'N%', 'calc(N% ± Mpx)', and keyword plus offset such as 'right 12px', meaning 100% - 12px, or 'bottom 8px'. d. For repeat / repeat-x / repeat-y, loop drawImage over the grid, offset by off modulo tile and clipped to the canvas. e. Export PNG via toPng. Because the bitmap matches the node exactly, FILL causes no distortion, and the box's corner radius clips it like CSS background-clip does. 5. 1. **Bevel styles (`inset`, `outset`, `groove`, `ridge`).** Replace each side's color with Chrome's shaded color. Calibrate the shading against the harness. For gray rgb(128) on white, the measured result for `inset` is top = 154 and bottom = 238.
   - Use a small helper `bevel(col, side, style)`.
   - For `inset` and `groove`, top and left get the "dark" variant and bottom and right get the "light" variant. `outset` and `ridge` swap them.
   - Treat the style as solid afterwards. `groove` and `ridge` at width ≥ 2 split into two half-width bands. Approximating each as a single band is acceptable.

2. **Same color on all sides.** If all painted sides now share one color and one style, return exactly what `borders()` returns today. No regression.

3. **Two colors in a box with no visible content area.** This covers `<hr>`: one dimension of the border box equals the sum of the borders on that axis, and there are no fills. Return `{ fillOverride: [solid(colorB)], stroke: { paint: solid(colorT), weights: { t: wT, r: 0, b: 0, l: 0 } } }`. For the default hr this gives a frame of height 2 with a fill of the bottom color and a 1px INSIDE top stroke of the top color, which is exact. Use the same trick on the vertical axis for vertical rules.

4. **Other cases where side colors differ** (e.g. `border border-gray-200 border-l-4 border-l-indigo-500`). Pick the most common painted color as the stroke paint, with weights only for the sides that have that color. For each remaining side, emit an extra overlay child:

   - code.js already handles `absolute`. It sets `layoutPositioning = 'ABSOLUTE'` only when the parent has a layoutMode, so this stays valid in the real API.
   - Insert the overlays after the content children so they are drawn on top. CSS borders sit outside the padding box, so content never overlaps them.
   - If any corner radius is non-zero, skip the overlays and keep the single majority-color stroke, because straight side rects cannot follow rounded corners.

5. **Leave code.js `applyBox` unchanged.** Per-side stroke weights, frame fills and absolute RECT children are all standard Figma API (`strokeTopWeight`, etc., `layoutPositioning`).
